t.1.132.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the great-souled Pāṇḍavas had been thus addressed by the king, the evil-minded Duryodhana was filled with the greatest joy.
t.1.132.2: Bull of the Bharatas, he led his minister Purocana to a secluded place, took him by the right hand, and spoke these words.
t.1.132.3: This earth, filled with wealth, is mine, Purocana; as it is mine, so it is yours as well, and you must protect it.
t.1.132.4: For I have no other ally more trustworthy than you, with whom, having come to an agreement, I could take counsel as I do with you.
t.1.132.6: The Pāṇḍavas, sent by Dhṛtarāṣṭra to Vāraṇāvata, will amuse themselves at the festival at Dhṛtarāṣṭra's command.
t.1.132.5: Guard this secret counsel, my dear friend, and root out my rivals by a skillful stratagem; do exactly as I tell you.
t.1.132.7: So act that you go to Vāraṇāvata this very day, in a swift-moving chariot yoked with donkeys.
t.1.132.8: Having gone there, you should have a four-halled house built, well enclosed and very costly, set close against the armory.
t.1.132.9: Hemp, resin of the sal tree, and whatever other inflammable substances there are here, have all of them supplied.
t.1.132.10: Mixing clay with ghee and oil and with a great quantity of lac, you should have a plaster of it applied to the walls.
t.1.132.11: Hemp, bamboo, ghee, wood, and various contrivances, all these you should place everywhere throughout that house.
t.1.132.13: When the house there has been made thus, you should honour them supremely and lodge the sons of Pāṇḍu there, along with Kuntī and her companions.
t.1.132.12: And it must be done in such a way that the Pāṇḍavas, even as they examine it, do not suspect you, thinking 'this is made to burn,' and that other men do not either.
t.1.132.14: There excellent seats, carriages and beds must be arranged for the Pāṇḍavas, so that my father may be pleased.
t.1.132.15: Everything must be arranged so that they may dwell happily and without suspicion in the city of Vāraṇāvata, until the time has come round.
t.1.132.16: But when you know that they are fully trusting, asleep, and fearing nothing from any quarter, then you must set fire to that house, starting from its door.
t.1.132.18: Having promised the Kaurava, "So be it," Purocana set out for the city of Vāraṇāvata in a vehicle yoked with donkeys.
t.1.132.17: Of the Pāṇḍavas thus burned in their own house, people or kinsmen will then say only, 'They were burned,' whenever they ever speak on the Pāṇḍavas' behalf.
t.1.132.19: Having gone there swiftly, O king, Purocana, abiding by Duryodhana's counsel, did everything just as the prince had instructed.
